messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated token verification failures detected for auth provider (external). Auto-paging oncall. Summary: ~40% auth verification 401s across frontend + API, console logins impacted. Investigate now.

maria (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a spike in 401s starting 1769801200. errors look like 'invalid_signature' from verification library.

maria (oncall): quick log snippet: ```ERROR auth.verify Token verify failed: invalid_signature - kid: abcd1234 - source: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json```

jordan (eng): yup same here from session-service metrics. KV cache for JWKS shows high miss rate and repeated fetches to auth provider.

sam (sre): paging Slack -> I'm joining. can you confirm customer-facing impact: console vs API vs background jobs?

kai (support): getting multiple customer DMs saying they can't log in to console; some report 401 on API calls from mobile apps. Support queue spiking.

maria (oncall): rough numbers: 40% of interactive logins failing, ~12% of API requests erroring with 401, backlog for support up ~3x. Affected regions: us-east and eu-west.

jordan (eng): investigating JWKS fetch pattern. auth provider appears to be rotating keys aggressively; our verifier library fails on signatures for recently issued tokens until new JWKS is fetched. repeated fetches hitting rate limits.

sam (sre): ok, immediate mitigation options: 1) extend local JWKS TTL to avoid hammering provider (short term), 2) use cached fallback of last-known key for verification, 3) route traffic to a fallback auth-verifier (if we have one), 4) degrade console to read-only while we fix.

maria (oncall): I'll flip TTL on the cache to 15m from 1m and enable last-known-key acceptance for an hour. Jordan, can you push the change?

jordan (eng): pushing a config change to session-service config store now. deploying to canary first. command: ```curl -XPOST https://config.redwood.internal/kv -d '{"session.jwks_ttl":900, "session.accept_stale_kid":true}'```

deploy-bot: deploy started: session-service/config-rollout v2 -> canary (maria approved)

maria (oncall): canary looks good, no increase in errors there after change. rolling to 50%.

kai (support): customers on older mobile builds are still failing, likely cached tokens with new signatures. Any suggestion for support replies?

sam (sre): ask affected customers to retry after 5-10m. We're accepting slightly stale keys for now so many should be able to log in. If they still fail, escalate to support@redwood and include trace ids.

jordan (eng): also adding a short-term rate-limit on JWKS fetches per host to avoid provider throttling. patching client code now.

maria (oncall): Auth provider status page shows partial degradation: "We are investigating a key rotation service issue causing intermittent JWT verification failures". They claim a fix is in progress.

sam (sre): good to know. I'm going to declare this Sev2 (customer-impacting but partial) and start a postmortem after recovery. Noting timeline and mitigations.

maria (oncall): updating customers on status page + support templates. drafting message: "We're seeing intermittent login failures due to third-party auth key rotations. We're applying temporary verification fallbacks and expect restoration within 30-60 minutes. No account data compromised." suggestions?

kai (support): add: "If you are logged in, please avoid logging out until we confirm resolution" and include workaround steps for CLI/API: refresh token retry pattern.

jordan (eng): added fallback logic in two more services (console-proxy and mobile-token-checker). rolling now.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: session-service/config-rollout v2 -> 100% (deployed at 1769801458)

maria (oncall): errors dropping to ~8% in us-east, eu-west trending down. support ticket creation rate stabilizing.

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled in 40 minutes. current owner: maria (oncall).

sam (sre): maria, I'll take the handoff at +40. please drop a runbook pointer and key facts.

maria (oncall): runbook link: https://intranet/redwood/incidents/runbooks/auth-jwks-rotation (added) — key facts: external provider rotated keys aggressively, caused signature mismatches; we enabled stale-key acceptance, increased JWKS TTL, and rate-limited JWKS fetches. Monitor 401 rate and support queue.

kai (support): support template posted to #support-templates. copy: "We're aware of login errors for some customers. We're applying temporary verification fallbacks; please retry in 10 minutes. If you continue to experience issues, reply with trace id and platform."

jordan (eng): auth provider reports they've deployed a fix at 1769801520 and are propagating stable keys. recommend we revert stale-key acceptance after 30m and gradually return TTL to default.

maria (oncall): agree. I'll start reverting the temporary accepts at +30m after propagation check.

sam (sre): I'll keep an eye on latency and 401 counts, and follow up with a brief incident summary to ops and product.

maria (oncall): reverting accept_stale_kid=false in session-service in 10m. will post when complete.

maria (oncall): revert done. session-service rolled (1769801605). monitoring now. 401s back down to baseline ~0.5%.

kai (support): support queue cleared for auth-related issues. customers updated via status page and direct replies.

jordan (eng): creating a short-term mitigation library: add jittered backoff and exponential retry on token refreshes, persist last-known valid JWKS for cold starts, and a metric for JWKS rotation frequency. PR opened.

sam (sre): good. capture TODOs for postmortem: - why did our JWKS cache TTL default to 1m? - add dashboard for JWKS fetch success/fail and rate limit errors - consider signed key rotation window policy with auth providers - runbook update.

maria (oncall): handing off to sam for overnight watch. leaving notes in incident doc.

sam (sre): taking over. marking incident resolved for active mitigation; will schedule postmortem and follow-ups. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation successful, auth verification failures remediated. Incident status: monitoring -> resolved (mitigated)."
